ordered_diagnoses: Multisystem Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis with cutaneous manifestations

s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic multisystem disorder with skin manifestations and endocrine abnormalities
salient_findings: Numerous asymptomatic reddish-brownish papules, nodules, and plaques over the whole body
Central diabetes insipidus, growth retardation, and hypothyroidism
key_facts: 7-year medical history of skin lesions
Skin lesions began on bilateral eyelid margins and extended to trunk and extremities
Patient has central diabetes insipidus
Patient has growth retardation
Patient has hypothyroidism
Skin biopsy showed dense granulomatous infiltrate in the upper dermis
Immunohistochemical results were negative for CD1a and S-100, positive for CD68

Skin lesions are present on periocular areas, perioral areas, neck, shoulder, axillary folds, cubital fossa, wrists, palms, umbilical region, lateral abdomen, inguinal area, anogenital area, popliteal fossa, and ankles

shortlist.label: Erdheim-Chester Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Matches chronic multisystem disorder with skin manifestations and endocrine abnormalities, and specific biopsy findings

shortlist.label: Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with skin lesions, diabetes insipidus, and growth retardation, despite negative CD1a and S-100

shortlist.label: Multisystem Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis with cutaneous manifestations
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis but with multisystem involvement, fitting the patient's complex presentation

shortlist.label: Necrobiotic Xanthogranuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches skin lesions and potential endocrine abnormalities, with granulomatous infiltrate on biopsy

shortlist.label: Adult-Onset Multisystem Histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Fits the patient's multisystem disease with skin and endocrine involvement, and histiocytic infiltration on biopsy

raw.rationale: The patient's 7-year medical history of numerous asymptomatic reddish-brownish papules, nodules, and plaques, along with the presence of central diabetes insipidus, growth retardation, and hypothyroidism, are consistent with Erdheim-Chester Disease. The skin biopsy findings of a dense granulomatous infiltrate in the upper dermis and immunohistochemical results positive for CD68 also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
rejected.why: Immunohistochemical results were negative for CD1a and S-100, which are typically positive in Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis.

rejected.label: Multisystem Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis with cutaneous manifestations
rejected.why: Same reason as Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis, negative CD1a and S-100 results do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Necrobiotic Xanthogranuloma
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and biopsy findings do not match those typically seen in Necrobiotic Xanthogranuloma, which often involves the periorbital area but lacks the systemic involvement seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Adult-Onset Multisystem Histiocytosis
rejected.why: While this condition can present with similar skin findings, the presence of central diabetes insipidus, growth retardation, and hypothyroidism, along with the specific biopsy and immunohistochemical results, make Erdheim-Chester Disease a more likely diagnosis.
